summary: The exact candidate is a working bounded optimization for repeated identical Qwen image requests, but it does not provide the original explicit save/load-by-ID contract. Its regression and focused compatibility tests pass, while independent adversarial checks reproduce prompt-scoped keys, process-local storage, absent explicit API operations, and video/audio bypass. The candidate honestly documents these semantic limits, but its committed diff-check claim is contradicted by trailing whitespace in two raw logs.

tests.what_was_measured: At the recorded base, the imported Qwen processor came from /job/repo, had no request cache-key method, did not reference the preprocess cache, and called load_mm_data directly.
The exact candidate's cache-hit, single-flight, identity-scoping, bypass, and defensive-copy regression coverage; 4 tests passed.

The same content ID under a changed prompt generated a different key and two computations; a fresh processor recomputed; video/audio returned no key; Chat Completions and Responses exposed no explicit preprocessing save/load fields.
Focused cache, identity, parser, and OpenAI protocol compatibility; 115 tests and 30 subtests passed.
Candidate patch whitespace integrity; trailing whitespace was found in two committed raw pytest logs, contradicting the candidate report's claimed passing diff check.

gpu_evidence: The prepared stack reports torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2, but no qualifying Qwen-VL weights were available; no GPU result is used as evidence.
remaining_counterexamples: The same saved image content ID cannot reuse preprocessing when the rendered prompt changes because prompt text is part of the cache key.
There is no OpenAI API operation to explicitly save a preprocessing result and later load it by a caller-selected ID.
Cache entries are owned by each processor/tokenizer-worker process and are not shared across workers or preserved across restart.
Qwen video and audio requests explicitly bypass the new cache path.
remaining_limitations: No qualifying Qwen-VL model weights were available, so end-to-end Qwen semantic equivalence and preprocessing performance were not validated.
The tiny Llama serving fixture cannot validate Qwen architecture-specific preprocessing, cross-worker sharing, or restart persistence.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
The candidate's committed raw pytest logs contain trailing whitespace even though its report claims git diff --check passed.
